text:
marta: quick check-in — ran sq (activation-aware) quant on the new 13B longctx build (32k / 128k profiles). overall token-level LF drops are small on short prompts, but for >40k context we see a steady accuracy drift and KV-cache mismatches vs fp16. curious if others have seen this pattern with AWQ/GPTQ mixes. attaching quick notes and sample outputs.

chris: hmm. do you have the eval harness prompts + exact quant commands? could be an act-scale mismatch or blockwise scale overflow. also check layernorm eps changes when exporting.

marta: here's the run command and the failing eval snippet:

```
# quant run
python quantize.py --model-dir /models/13b-longctx --method smoothquant --bits 8 --act-aware true --calib-samples 2048 --out /tmp/13b-sq-awq

# eval (streaming long prompt)
python eval_longctx.py --model /tmp/13b-sq-awq --prompt-file tests/long-40k.prompts --max-tokens 12000
```

liam: quick thought — when we do mixed AWQ/GPTQ blocks, the activation distribution can shift for deep layers at high seq len. i saw something similar where top-3 tokens diverged after 50k because kv indices rolled in slightly different buckets. easiest probe: dump per-layer activation max/min during the failing run. use this snippet:

```
# enable dumping
export DUMP_ACT=1
python eval_longctx.py --model /tmp/13b-sq-awq --prompt-file tests/long-40k.prompts
# outputs -> /tmp/act_dumps/
```

jen: another angle — check runtime kvcache eviction policy. our runtime currently keeps fixed shard sizes and sometimes forces early eviction on >64k sequences which changes the prefix semantics. if eviction timestamp differs between fp16 and quantized kernels you'd see content drift. can you repro with cache disabled (slow but isolates)?

marta: good point, jen. i just re-ran with kvcache disabled and the mismatch drops by ~60%, but perplexity is still slightly worse than fp16. logs:

```
fp16 -> ppl 9.3
sq-awq -> ppl 10.1 (kvcache on)
sq-awq -> ppl 9.6 (kvcache off)
```

arjun: sounds like two things: (1) quantized kernels change micro-timing -> cache evictions, and (2) activation magnitudes drifting cause quant bins to clip. hypothesis: activation outliers in attention Q/K produce large dynamic range that AWQ's block scales don't capture for 128k. try act clipping + layerwise rescale during export. e.g.

```
# export with act clipping
python export.py --model /models/13b-longctx --smoothquant --clip-acts 6.0 --rescale-layernorm true
```

liam: for experiments i'd suggest a matrix: {fp16, fp8, int8-gptq, int8-awq} x {kvcache on/off} x {clip none/6.0/4.0}. small sample grid (18 runs) should tell which factor dominates. also add the "zero-prefix" test where you prepend N zeros to make sure drift isn't prompt-dependent.

marta: thanks, will run that matrix. two quick asks: (A) can someone share the eval harness config (prompt sets + metrics) we should use so i'm consistent? (B) any quick dev infra to run the grid in parallel on dev-gpu-pool?

chris: i'll drop the eval harness bundle into /shared/eng-ml/longctx-harness.tar.gz this afternoon. it contains the prompt sets, token-level aligner, and a regen script.

deploy-bot: deployment status: dev-gpu-pool has 6 available nodes (A100s). quota for parallel jobs per-user = 4. Use --parallel=4 on the grid runner.

jen: also add a small regression eval (SQuAD-like QA and a summarization accuracy set) — sometimes ppl hides correctness regressions. if you can run those in the matrix, great.

marta: perfect. i'll kick off the 18-run grid with kvcache on/off + clip levels, land outputs in /artifacts/13b-actdrift/ and upload act dumps. will report back with per-layer deltas and a short hypothesis doc. thanks all :thumbsup:

chris: great — if you see persistent mismatch even after clipping, ping me and we'll try blockwise re-calibration at export time (recompute quant scales on a per-layer per-token basis).
